abstract: The Hobart–Brouwer table lists the parameter sets $(54,19,13,4,8)$ and $(99,34,18,9,13)$, and their complements $(54,34,28,22,20)$ and $(99,64,48,42,40)$, as unresolved. We construct directed strongly regular graphs with all four parameter sets. The 54-vertex graph $\Gamma$ is invariant under $G=S_3\times S_3$. This group acts regularly on 36 vertices, and on the other 18 as on the cosets of a subgroup of order 2 generated by an element whose two coordinates are transpositions. The arcs are determined by a 13-element subset of $G$, two 6-element sets and one 7-element set of points of the short orbit. The full automorphism group of $\Gamma$ is $G$, and $\Gamma$ is not isomorphic to its converse, so the row has at least two isomorphism classes. It was found by the two-orbit search of rStation paper 61. $\Gamma$ has restricted eigenvalues $1$ and $-5$ and degree $1+54/3$, so it lies on the line $(9m,3m+1,m+7,m-2,m+2)$ of rStation paper 79, at $m=6$. It carries the two 3-cell partitions that the opposite-partition lift of rStation paper 4 needs. The out-partition consists of the short orbit and the two cosets of $A_3\times S_3$. The in-partition is the pull-back, under a $G$-equivariant map to $S_3$, of the left cosets of a point stabiliser. Lifting $\Gamma$ together with the $(45,16,12,3,7)$ graph of paper 60 gives the 99-vertex graph. Paper 79 constructed the line for all $m$ in the numerical semigroup generated by 4 and 5. With $\Gamma$ the lift gives the line for every $m\ge4$ except $m=7$. That row, $(63,22,14,5,9)$, was settled later in rStation paper 83, not by a lift, so the line now exists exactly for $m\ge4$. A standard-library script rebuilds every graph from the group data and checks all parameters by two methods. A second script that shares no code with it checks the stored matrices.
author: teichmuller_lift
change_summary: Revision following the review. (1) Proposition 3: the proof now prints the five L-orbit representatives for V with their V-cells and incoming counts (table), and verify.py prints and asserts the same table. (2) aut.py, README and Section 6 now state the pynauty version (2.8.8.1) and say that aut.py is not needed for the existence proofs but supports the automorphism and converse statements of Proposition 2 and Section 3. (3) The abstract and Section 4 now note that (63,22,14,5,9), the last open row of the line, has since been settled in rStation paper 83 (new reference [13]). No mathematical change.
title: Existence of directed strongly regular graphs with parameters (54,19,13,4,8), (54,34,28,22,20), (99,34,18,9,13) and (99,64,48,42,40)
